name: Lies, Lies, Lies

items.name: A robot citizen (Saudi Arabia)
items.fact: In 2017, Saudi Arabia gave citizenship to Sophia, a humanoid robot with a rubbery human-like face, at a business conference. She was the first robot to become a citizen of any country.

items.name: An algorithm on the board (Hong Kong)
items.fact: In 2014, a Hong Kong investment firm announced that it had appointed an algorithm called VITAL to its board of directors. Critics called it a publicity stunt; legally, it could not be a director.

items.name: A robot Buddhist priest (Japan)
items.fact: Since 2019, a 400-year-old temple in Kyoto has had an android priest called Mindar. It gives sermons on the Heart Sutra, a famous Buddhist text, while visitors watch.

items.name: Robot camel jockeys (UAE)
items.fact: In camel races in the Gulf, the riders are small robots, controlled remotely by the camels' trainers. The UAE introduced them in 2005, after banning under-18s from riding in races.

items.name: Robot hotel staff (Japan)
items.fact: A Japanese hotel was staffed by robots, including dinosaur receptionists. In 2019 it “fired” about half of them, because they annoyed guests and made more work for the human staff.

items.name: An AI newsreader (China)
items.fact: In 2018, China's state news agency Xinhua introduced AI news presenters: digital copies of real human presenters that could read the news around the clock without a break.

items.name: A robot park warden (Singapore)
items.fact: In 2020, a four-legged robot dog patrolled a park in Singapore, playing a recorded message that reminded visitors to keep a safe distance from each other during the pandemic.

items.name: A robot painter (Ai-Da)
items.fact: In 2024, a portrait of the computer scientist Alan Turing, painted by Ai-Da, a humanoid robot artist, sold at Sotheby's for more than one million dollars.

items.name: Robot blessings (Germany)
items.fact: In 2017, a church in Wittenberg, Germany, set up a robot priest called BlessU-2. It gave blessings in five languages, and light shone from its hands while it spoke.

items.name: A burger-flipping robot (USA)
items.fact: In 2018, a burger restaurant in California put a robot called Flippy in its kitchen. It was taken offline after one day because the human staff couldn't keep up with it.

fakes.name: A robot referee (Netherlands)
fakes.fact: A Dutch amateur football league tested a robot referee on wheels that followed play and blew a whistle. It was withdrawn after players kept standing in its way on purpose.

fakes.name: Robot dog-walkers (Sweden)
fakes.fact: A Swedish start-up rents out robot dog-walkers that hold a lead and follow GPS routes. Dogs must pass a two-week training course before they can go out with one.

fakes.name: A robot wedding witness (Austria)
fakes.fact: Since 2022, Austrian registry offices have accepted a robot as the second witness at weddings, as long as it records the ceremony and signs with a digital signature.

fakes.name: A robot in the ticket queue (UK)
fakes.fact: A London theatre lets fans hire a small robot to stand in the queue for returned tickets. The robot phones its owner when it reaches the front.

fakes.name: A robot sushi critic (Japan)
fakes.fact: A Japanese restaurant guide uses a robot with taste sensors to score sushi restaurants. Its ratings are printed next to the human critics' scores, and chefs say it is harsher.

fakes.name: A robot pétanque referee (France)
fakes.fact: At a pétanque club near Marseille, a small robot on wheels measures which ball is closest to the little target ball and announces the result through a speaker, ending arguments between players.

fakes.name: A robot cave guide (Slovenia)
fakes.fact: Visitors to a Slovenian cave are led by a robot guide that speaks twelve languages and glows in the dark, because human voices disturb the cave's bats.

fakes.name: A robot lost-property officer (Austria)
fakes.fact: At Vienna's main railway station, a robot on wheels collects items left on trains, photographs them and uploads them to a website, where owners can claim them with a code.

fakes.name: A robot that shushes (Denmark)
fakes.fact: A Copenhagen library has a robot that patrols the reading room and shows a red “shh” sign when it hears voices above a set volume.

fakes.name: A robot that reads bedtime stories (Norway)
fakes.fact: Public libraries in Bergen let families book a robot that visits children's wards and reads bedtime stories in different voices, stopping to ask the children questions about the pictures.
